scope.title: Work done by a constant force: W=Fs cosθ, sign of work, zero work
excluded: work_energy_theorem as a separate learning objective
scope.beyond_grade9: Beyond Grade 9, given: comparing work measured in two constant-velocity inertial frames (W01-A5, CYCLE-FRAME, MIS06, SCN05); Grade 9 calculations use only the ground frame; non-inertial frames are excluded.

shared_inferential_jump: To determine work, identify the force and body, use that body’s displacement in a declared frame, resolve the constant force along that displacement to obtain its signed work (including zero cases), and add the signed contributions of all forces acting on the body.

academic_truth_from.status: Canonical Physics library reports CANDIDATE; this pair is a draft projection for the syllabus tile, not an admitted library change.

truth_sources.use: Fs cosθ definition, sign and zero-work contrasts

conventions.statement: Identify the body whose displacement is measured and name each force acting ON that same body; label who exerts each force.
Specify the observation interval and use the ground frame; displacement is final position minus initial position in ground coordinates.
In this tile, every contributing force is constant in magnitude and direction over one straight displacement; use the force on the body and that body’s displacement in the same frame.
Use s ≥ 0 for displacement magnitude (m), F ≥ 0 for force magnitude (N), θ between their directions from 0° through 180°, and a fixed right/up axis when components are used.
The signed component along displacement is F_parallel=F cosθ, hence W=F_parallel s=Fs cosθ; the sign is the sign of that component.
For s>0, a force perpendicular to displacement has zero work despite force and motion; if s=0, every constant-force contribution is zero.
For several forces acting on the SAME body through the SAME displacement, total work is their signed sum, W_total=ΣW_i. A force on another body does not belong in this sum.
Units: 1 J=1 N·m. The work of an individual force may be negative, zero or positive; force magnitude and displacement magnitude cannot be negative.
No claim of frictionlessness unless stated. Normal reaction, friction, tension and gravity are accounted for by their actual components; do not infer they vanish from an object label.
Treat every modelled body as rigid and undergoing straight translation without deformation or rotation over the stated interval, unless explicitly stated otherwise; use the ground frame for Grade 9.

microtopic.title: Constant-force work: assign force/body/frame, project, sign and add
microtopic.secondary_capability_note: Signed addition of force contributions taught without deriving the work-energy theorem.
microtopic.badge_reason: The difficult selection is the relevant body and displacement angle, not the multiplication; multiple forces and zero-work counterexamples expose it.
entry_assumptions: Can distinguish a force from its magnitude and draw a direction arrow (Newton’s laws / free-body diagrams).
Can name the agent and target of a force; Newton’s third law acts on different bodies.
Can identify start/end positions, displacement direction and magnitude in metres in a selected ground frame.
Can use horizontal/vertical components and basic cosines: cos0°=1, cos60°=1/2, cos90°=0, cos120°=−1/2, cos180°=−1.
Can add positive and negative signed numbers and multiply N by m to obtain J.
Can distinguish force remaining constant during one straight displacement from a varying force, without calculus.
Use the ground frame throughout Grade 9; steady co-moving inertial-frame displacements are supplied only in the explicitly marked beyond Grade 9 extension.
Given contact/weight/friction forces may act even on a moving body; frictionlessness is never silently inferred.
microtopic.inferential_jump: To determine work, identify the force and body, use that body’s displacement in a declared frame, resolve the constant force along that displacement to obtain its signed work (including zero cases), and add the signed contributions of all forces acting on the body.

teaching_path.action: Choose the target body, force agent, actual initial/final positions, interval and frame before manipulating any equation.
teaching_path.why_valid: Work is indexed to a particular force on a particular body over a particular displacement; changing one changes the work being calculated.

teaching_path.action: Draw the body’s displacement arrow from start to finish; label its magnitude s and the fixed coordinate axis.
teaching_path.why_valid: The displacement arrow, not an assumed forward direction or distance walked, is what defines along and opposite for the constant-force calculation.

teaching_path.action: Draw the constant force arrow on that body and measure θ between the force and displacement arrows with tails brought together.
teaching_path.why_valid: The angle in the work relation is between the actual force and the actual displacement, not between a force and a convenient vertical/horizontal line.

teaching_path.action: Bring the force and displacement arrows to a common tail. Drop a perpendicular from the tip of the force arrow onto the line of displacement to make a right triangle. For an acute angle θ, the adjacent side divided by the hypotenuse is cosθ, so the along-displacement component has size Fcosθ; if θ is obtuse the projection points opposite displacement and the component is signed negative. Multiply that signed component by s to construct W=Fs cosθ.
teaching_path.why_valid: Right-triangle geometry gives adjacent/hypotenuse=cosθ; the perpendicular projection does not contribute along the straight displacement. The sign is determined by whether the component points with or against the displacement, including an obtuse-angle negative cosine.

teaching_path.action: Classify with θ: 0°≤θ<90° positive, θ=90° zero, 90°<θ≤180° negative for nonzero F and s.
teaching_path.why_valid: The cosine changes sign across 90°; no force orientation alone determines work if s=0.

teaching_path.action: Test two distinct zero cases: moving level while supported by a vertical normal force, and a stationary object with a horizontal applied force.
teaching_path.why_valid: One has nonzero displacement but no along-displacement force component; the other has no displacement despite a force.

teaching_path.action: For several forces on the same body, calculate each signed work for the same interval and add: W_total=W_1+W_2+⋯.
teaching_path.why_valid: Work of forces is additive; positive and negative contributions may cancel without each individually vanishing.

teaching_path.action: Check units N×m=J, reverse the displacement while force direction stays fixed (work changes sign), and test s=0 or θ=90° as limits.
teaching_path.why_valid: Independent sign, zero and units tests catch mistakes that a numeric calculator alone will miss.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Every nonzero force acting while an object moves does positive work.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A suitcase moves horizontally while its supporting hand exerts a vertical upward force; is the hand’s work necessarily positive?
misconceptions.diagnostic_answer: No: for horizontal displacement, the vertical supporting force is perpendicular and does zero work.
misconceptions.repair: Put the displacement arrow beside the force arrow, resolve only the component parallel to it, and multiply that signed component by s.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: The angle in Fs cosθ is the angle to the horizontal axis even when the displacement is not horizontal.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A box rises vertically while an upward force acts. Is θ=90° because the force is perpendicular to the horizontal?
misconceptions.diagnostic_answer: No: force and displacement are both upward, so θ=0°.
misconceptions.repair: Move arrow tails together and measure the force–displacement angle, not the force–page or force–axis angle.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A negative work is impossible because F and s are positive magnitudes.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: An opposing force points left as an object moves right; what sets the work sign?
misconceptions.diagnostic_answer: cos180°=−1, so signed work is negative.
misconceptions.repair: Keep magnitudes nonnegative but retain the sign of F_parallel=Fcosθ.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Zero total work means no individual force did any work.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Two equal opposing horizontal forces act on a right-moving body; can their individual works be nonzero?
misconceptions.diagnostic_answer: Yes: one positive, one negative, and their signed sum zero.
misconceptions.repair: Show a row for each force; do not replace the ledger by a single zero row.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: A force exerted by the body on something else can be included as work done on the body.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: When a hand pulls a cart, is the force exerted by the cart on the hand part of the cart’s own-force work sum?
misconceptions.diagnostic_answer: No: it acts on the hand, not on the cart.
misconceptions.repair: For every force label write agent → target; retain only arrows whose target is the chosen body.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: The same numerical work must result in every frame, even though the body’s displacement changes.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: Beyond Grade 9, given: In one inertial frame a crate moves 3 m while in a supplied steady co-moving inertial frame its displacement is 0 m. With forces unchanged, must each individual work have the same value?
misconceptions.diagnostic_answer: No: the displacement is different across the two frames, so individual work can differ.
misconceptions.repair: Beyond Grade 9, given: use the stated displacement in each inertial frame when computing individual work; Grade 9 calculations stay in the ground frame.
misconceptions.extension_marker: beyond Grade 9, given: two steady inertial frames, with their displacements supplied.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: If an object stays put, the work of a nonzero applied force must still be Fs.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: A firm wall remains stationary under a constant push; what is s for the wall over the interval?
misconceptions.diagnostic_answer: s=0, hence the push does zero mechanical work on the wall in this model.
misconceptions.repair: Read actual displacement from the initial and final body positions before multiplying.

exit_task.prompt: A 2 kg rigid crate moves 5 m left along a horizontal straight floor in the ground frame. Four constant forces act ON the crate: a 12 N pull left, an 8 N drag right, an upward normal of 20 N, and a downward gravitational force of 20 N (g=10 m/s²). State the body, agents, frame, displacement, each force’s work, total work, and why the two vertical forces have zero work. No other forces act.

answer.summary: Pull +60 J; drag −40 J; normal 0 J; gravity 0 J; net +20 J.
reasoning: Target is the rigid crate; frame is ground; displacement is 5 m LEFT. All four listed forces act on the crate, including gravity downward.
Pull left with displacement left: θ=0°, W_pull=12×5=+60 J.
Drag right opposed to leftward displacement: θ=180°, W_drag=8×5×(−1)=−40 J.
Normal upward and gravity downward: θ=90° to horizontal displacement; both do 0 J.
Signed total=60−40+0+0=+20 J.
answer.check: Along-displacement resultant is 12−8=4 N left; 4×5=20 J. Units J.
acceptable_alternatives: A table of forces in the left-positive displacement axis with identical signed values.

microtopic.research_contribution: Original Grade 9 contrasts derived from canonical Work Direction and Work Constant Force records; OpenStax 7.1/7.2 consulted for independent treatment of sign, perpendicular force, and signed net work. No coaching/question-bank content copied.

predict.prompt: Several steady forces act on a rigid box undergoing a straight ground-frame displacement. What quantities and labels are needed to determine the work by each force and their total?
predict.defensible_answer: No. Each force must be assigned to the chosen body; work uses that force’s signed component along the body’s displacement in the chosen frame, and individual contributions must be added.

attempt.produces: Submit a complete signed-work report for a rigid body acted on by at least two constant forces during one straight ground-frame displacement: include the body and force-agent labels, start and finish positions, justified signed individual and total works (with units), an applicable zero-work case, and the stated model assumptions.
attempt.model_response: Choose one body and frame and one straight-displacement interval. For each constant force acting on that body, measure θ from the displacement direction, compute W_i=F_i s cosθ_i, include any zero work, then add the signed values. A force on a different body is excluded. If the body has s=0, each work is zero. Example of a non-numbered model ledger: one along, one opposed, and one perpendicular force give positive, negative and zero contributions respectively.

rubric.criterion: Declares target body, force agents, frame, interval, displacement and constant-force straight-line assumption.
rubric.evidence_of: The requested picture or labels identify all of these explicitly.

rubric.criterion: Relates each force’s work to the component and the actual displacement.
rubric.evidence_of: For every included force, defines θ relative to displacement and writes W_i=F_i s cosθ_i.

rubric.criterion: Explains at least one zero contribution without confusing zero force and zero work.
rubric.evidence_of: Perpendicular projection or zero displacement is cited in the completed explanation.

rubric.criterion: Adds the signed works and reports units.
rubric.evidence_of: One signed sum for same-body forces, with N·m=J.

accepted: A same-body work ledger with each force projection, signed contribution, zero possibility and total.
rejected: Add the work by the body on another object as though that force also acts on the chosen body. Incorrect: the target of that force is different.
Every nonzero force does positive work while the body moves. Incorrect: the angle can make it negative or zero.

route.ask: What body’s position changes in the chosen frame?
Which of the labelled forces actually act on that body?
route.why_this_ask: Exclude opposite-member force from a different body.
route.model_answer: Only the forces whose target is the chosen body.

route.ask: How do you compare each arrow to the displacement arrow?
route.why_this_ask: Construct the correct angle and component.
route.model_answer: Measure the angle between force and displacement, then project F along displacement.

route.ask: What must happen after each separate work has been found?
route.model_answer: Sum all same-body signed works and check joules.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Core1A reveals a fixed route and fully solved numeric examples; Core1B first requires the learner to design their own labelled force ledger, then reconstructs ownership, projection and summation from that commitment.

boundary_test.prompt: A moving trolley feels a 20 N upward normal while moving 8 m horizontally, and a separate 5 N forward drive. Can total work be zero merely because the normal does no work? Explain with one calculation.
boundary_test.answer: No. Normal work is 0 J, but the 5 N forward drive does +5×8=+40 J; if no other along-path force acts, total is +40 J.
boundary_test.confirms: Distinguishes zero work by one perpendicular force from total work by all forces.

relation.equation: W_i = F_i s cosθ_i = F_{i,parallel}s; W_total = Σ_i W_i
model_assumptions: Same target body, specified interval and displacement frame for each included force.
Each force constant in magnitude/direction over one straight displacement.
θ is the force/displacement angle; displacement magnitude s≥0, force magnitude F_i≥0.
Force/work of a different target body excluded.
For straight horizontal movement, gravity/normal have zero work only if genuinely perpendicular; no silent omission of friction.
relation.axis_and_sign: Choose displacement as positive along-path direction; along component positive, opposing negative, perpendicular zero. θ∈[0°,180°].
relation.physical_interpretation: Work of a constant force on a body measures the signed contribution of that force along the body’s displacement. It is not force magnitude, exertion, or the work of a different body.
checks: Sum individual works before inferring the total.
Reverse displacement with all forces held fixed: each work changes sign.
A work result must report joules and the same body/frame/interval.

core1a.title: Constant-force work: completed construction

ordered_blocks.show: Work by constant forces on the same body, declared displacement and inertial frame; straight segments only.

questions.title: An inclined tow force makes horizontal work
questions.setup: On a horizontal straight section, a sled moves 5 m right in the ground frame. A rope exerts a constant 18 N on the sled at 60° above the rightward displacement. Find the rope’s work only. No other forces are being evaluated in this example.

reasoning: Target=the sled; agent=rope. Its displacement is 5 m right in the ground frame.
θ is measured between the rope force and the rightward displacement: 60°.
The parallel component is 18cos60°=9 N to the right; the perpendicular part does not contribute to the horizontal displacement.
W_rope=(9 N)(5 m)=+45 J. Positive sign means the component is along displacement.
A dimensional check gives N·m=J.
answer.summary: The rope does +45 J of work on the sled.
answer.check: If the rope became vertical while the sled displacement stayed horizontal, its work would be 0 J.

questions.title: Zero work even while a trolley moves
questions.setup: A 3 kg trolley rolls 6 m right on a horizontal straight track in the ground frame; the track’s normal force on it remains 30 N upward and its weight is 30 N downward (take g=10 m/s²). Calculate the work by each vertical force. Ignore any horizontal forces here; no claim of frictionlessness is needed.

reasoning: Choose the trolley as the body and 6 m right as its displacement.
The track normal points up and weight points down; each is perpendicular to the horizontal displacement.
For either vertical force, θ=90° and cosθ=0.
W_normal=30×6×0=0 J and W_weight=30×6×0=0 J, although both forces and motion exist.
These results do not claim zero work by possible horizontal forces.
answer.summary: Normal and weight individually do zero work for this horizontal displacement.
answer.check: If the trolley rose vertically by 1 m instead, gravity would do negative work and the vertical normal’s work would depend on the force actually exerted.

questions.title: Several forces: a signed work ledger
questions.setup: A block slides 4 m right in the ground frame. A horizontal motor-pull force of 15 N acts right, a constant resistive force of 4 N acts left, and normal and weight act vertically. The surface is horizontal; all forces remain constant during the interval. Calculate work by each and their total.

reasoning: All forces must act on the SAME block over the SAME 4 m displacement in the ground frame.
Pull: θ=0°, W_pull=15×4=+60 J.
Resistance: θ=180°, W_resistance=4×4×(−1)=−16 J.
Normal and weight: θ=90°, so each contributes 0 J.
Sum the signed rows: W_total=60−16+0+0=+44 J. This is the total work, not the work by the motor alone.
answer.summary: Individual works +60 J, −16 J, 0 J, 0 J; total +44 J.
answer.check: Along-path net force is 15−4=11 N; (11 N)(4 m)=44 J as an independent recomputation.

questions.title: A push with no displacement
questions.setup: A horizontal 50 N push acts on a rigid block secured to a rigid wall. During a 3 s interval in the ground frame, the block and its contact point stay fixed. Calculate the work of this push on the block; the wall provides whatever balancing reaction is needed.

reasoning: The target is the block; the applied force is 50 N right.
The actual initial and final positions are equal, so the displacement magnitude is s=0 m.
Constant-force work is W=Fs cosθ; multiplying by s=0 gives W_push=0 J regardless of force magnitude.
The person may exert effort, but that is not mechanical work ON the motionless block through displacement.
answer.summary: The push does 0 J of mechanical work on the fixed block.
answer.check: If the contact point moved 0.2 m right under a constant 50 N rightward force, the same model would give +10 J.

questions.title: Beyond Grade 9, given: whose displacement and which inertial frame?
questions.setup: BEYOND GRADE 9, GIVEN (no derivation of moving-frame physics): A crate rides steadily on a horizontal vehicle. During 2 s the crate moves 2 m right in the ground frame. Two constant, balanced horizontal forces act on it: belt contact 5 N right and an opposing resistive force 5 N left. Compare work by these forces in the ground frame with that in the frame moving steadily with the crate. The two frames are inertial; there is no relative crate displacement in the second frame.

reasoning: Choose the crate, not the belt or vehicle, as the target of both forces.
Ground frame: s=2 m right; belt contact does +5×2=+10 J, resistance does −5×2=−10 J; sum 0 J.
Steady co-moving frame: the same crate has s=0 m for the same 2 s; each constant-force work is 0 J in this frame.
The individual work values differ because displacement differs across the frames; the net work is 0 J in both for these balanced forces.
No change in force magnitudes is assumed; only the described inertial coordinate frame differs.
answer.summary: Ground: +10 J and −10 J (net zero). Co-moving: 0 J and 0 J (net zero).
answer.check: Report force agent, target body, interval and frame with every work value. Otherwise numbers from different frames can be mixed incorrectly.

questions.scope_marker: beyond Grade 9, given: steady co-moving inertial-frame comparison; the specified displacements are provided.

scope_guards: Grade 9: basic components/cosines only; no calculus, integrals or arbitrary curved displacement.
Grade 9 uses only the ground frame. The optional W01-A5 comparison of two constant-velocity inertial frames is beyond Grade 9, given; no non-inertial frame is used.
All anchors are authored concept examples, not exam questions.

core1b.title: Constant-force work: predict, attempt, reconstruct, repair

ordered_blocks.text: Work of constant forces on a chosen body; commit to each attempt before revealing the relevant answer.

ordered_blocks.resolution: Allowlist only; do not project the entire bucket.conventions.

predict.prompt: A rigid sled moves 4 m right in the ground frame while a brake pad exerts a constant 12 N force on it at 120° to its rightward displacement. What is the brake pad’s work on the sled?
predict.defensible_answer: The brake pad does −24 J on the sled: the component along the 4 m displacement is 12cos120°=−6 N.

attempt.produces: Give a justified signed ground-frame work result in joules for the brake pad on the sled, showing the target, force agent, displacement, stated angle and enough calculation to check your sign.
attempt.model_response: Target: sled; agent: brake pad; ground-frame displacement 4 m right; angle from displacement to pad force is 120°. The projected force is 12cos120°=−6 N, so W=−6×4=−24 J. This force does negative work on the sled.

rubric.criterion: Declares target, agent, frame, displacement and force–displacement angle.
rubric.evidence_of: Sled; brake pad; ground frame; 4 m right; θ=120°.

rubric.criterion: Computes work using the correct component and sign.
rubric.evidence_of: Signed component −6 N; work −24 J.

rubric.criterion: Gives units and a reason for the component.
rubric.evidence_of: Uses joules and a justified signed force–displacement calculation.

accepted: The brake pad does −24 J on the sled over the ground-frame 4 m rightward displacement.
rejected: The pad force does +48 J because its magnitude is 12 N and the sled moves 4 m. Incorrect: the force makes an obtuse 120° angle with displacement and gives −24 J.

route.ask: Which body is displaced?
Which angle is actually specified between arrows?
route.why_this_ask: Prevent measuring to a different reference direction.

route.ask: Which force component lies along the displacement?
route.why_this_ask: Elicit projection instead of supplying the result in advance.

route.ask: How does that signed component determine work?

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Core1A fully solves an acute-angle forward pull; Core1B asks the learner to determine the sign and size of work from an obtuse-angle braking force before revealing any projected force.

boundary_test.prompt: With the 12 N force and 4 m displacement unchanged, the pad-force direction is instead 60° to the rightward displacement. Compute its work and explain what changed.
boundary_test.answer: 12×4×cos60°=+24 J. Only the force–displacement angle changed; the signed component reversed sign.
boundary_test.confirms: Changing the angle across 90° reverses the work sign even when the force and displacement magnitudes do not change.

predict.prompt: A student pushes a movable board rightward; the board pushes the student leftward with an equal-sized contact force. Which of these forces belongs in an account of work done ON the board?
predict.defensible_answer: Include only the student’s push ON the board; the equal force exerted by the board ON the student acts on a different body and cannot be entered as work on the board.

attempt.produces: Produce the ground-frame force-ownership decision for work ON the board, identifying the board’s displacement, both agent→target arrows, and explaining which contribution belongs in its work ledger.
attempt.model_response: Choose the board. Student→board acts on the board and belongs in its work account; board→student acts on the student and must not be entered as work on the board. The board’s ground-frame displacement is rightward. Magnitudes need not be given to classify ownership.

rubric.criterion: Names the target and each agent→target force.
rubric.evidence_of: Target board; student→board and board→student are distinct force-body pairs.

rubric.criterion: Keeps only the force on the chosen body.
rubric.evidence_of: Include student→board, exclude board→student.

rubric.criterion: Names displacement and frame.
rubric.evidence_of: Board displacement rightward in the ground frame.

accepted: For work ON the board, include the student’s force on the board, not the board’s force on the student.
rejected: Both action–reaction forces are forces on the board, so include both. Incorrect: one acts on the student.

route.ask: What is the target body?
What does each contact-force arrow act on?
route.why_this_ask: Identify agents and targets rather than magnitudes.
route.model_answer: Student pushes board; board pushes student.

route.ask: Which displacement belongs in the selected work ledger?
route.model_answer: Board displacement in the ground frame.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Core1A lists force-by-force work for one body; here the learner discriminates which members of an interaction pair even belong in the ledger.

boundary_test.prompt: A hand exerts a constant 9 N force rightward on a rigid board that translates 2 m right on level ground. The board simultaneously exerts an equal leftward force on the hand. Calculate the hand-on-board work and explain whether the board-on-hand force should enter the board’s total-work ledger.
boundary_test.answer: Hand-on-board work is +9×2=+18 J. The board-on-hand force acts on the hand and must not be counted as work on the board; other board forces, if any, would be added separately.
boundary_test.confirms: The learner computes a named-force work and justifies body ownership instead of answering a memorised yes/no prompt.

predict.prompt: A passenger carries a 4 kg shopping bag 7 m horizontally at constant height in the ground frame while exerting a constant 40 N upward support force (g=10 m/s²). Could that support force have nonzero work on the bag for this interval?
predict.defensible_answer: No. The hand’s upward 40 N force is perpendicular to the bag’s horizontal 7 m ground-frame displacement, so its work is 0 J.

attempt.produces: Give the signed work by the hand and by gravity on the bag over the specified interval, showing the target, agents, ground-frame displacement, force–displacement angles, units and physical explanation.
attempt.model_response: Target: bag. The hand exerts 40 N upward; the bag moves 7 m horizontally at fixed height in ground frame. θ=90°, so hand work=40×7×cos90°=0 J. Weight=40 N downward, also perpendicular and does 0 J. The existence of force and motion does not make the work nonzero.

rubric.criterion: Declares target, agent, frame and displacement.
rubric.evidence_of: Bag, hand, ground, 7 m horizontally.

rubric.criterion: Computes hand and gravity work separately.
rubric.evidence_of: Both 0 J because their arrows are perpendicular to displacement.

rubric.criterion: Explains why motion and force can coexist with zero work.
rubric.evidence_of: Force component parallel to the displacement is zero.

accepted: Support and weight each do 0 J despite the 7 m horizontal movement.
rejected: Because the hand pushes upward with 40 N while the bag moves, its work is +280 J. Incorrect: θ=90°, so the parallel component is zero.

route.ask: What does the bag’s displacement arrow look like?
route.why_this_ask: Do not confuse position change with force direction.

route.ask: What is the orientation of the hand’s arrow?
What does that mean for work?
route.model_answer: Each vertical force has zero parallel component and zero work.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Core1A gives a trolley’s two vertical-force zero results; this cycle asks the learner to distinguish the displacement of a held bag from the direction of support and verify with a changed path.

boundary_test.prompt: The passenger steps upward 1 m carrying the bag while continuing to hold 40 N upward. What is the hand’s work on that segment?
boundary_test.answer: +40 J for the 1 m upward segment.
boundary_test.confirms: Changing the displacement direction can change work even when force magnitude is unchanged.

predict.prompt: A 75 N horizontal push acts rightward on a rigid cabinet that stays fixed against a solid stop for 6 s in the ground frame. What work does the push do on the cabinet during the 6 s?
predict.defensible_answer: 0 J: the cabinet has zero ground-frame displacement despite the 75 N push.

attempt.produces: Submit the signed work in joules by the pusher on the cabinet, specifying target, agent, ground-frame interval, displacement and a physical explanation; show a calculation using consistent units.
attempt.model_response: The target is the rigid cabinet and the agent is the pusher. It stays at the same ground-frame position over 6 s, so s=0 m and the push work is W=75 N×0 m=0 J. The 6 s duration is not a displacement.

rubric.criterion: States force agent, target, ground-frame interval and displacement.
rubric.evidence_of: Pusher on rigid cabinet; ground frame, 6 s; zero displacement.

rubric.criterion: Calculates the signed work and supplies correct units and reasoning.
rubric.evidence_of: W=75 N×0 m=0 J because displacement vanishes, even with a force.

accepted: The 75 N push does 0 J on the cabinet since it does not move in the ground frame.
rejected: The pusher does 450 J because 75 N acts for 6 s. Incorrect: 6 s is a duration, not a displacement; s=0 m makes work zero.

route.ask: What body’s position is being compared in the ground frame?
route.why_this_ask: The learner chooses a target and frame before calculating.

route.ask: Where was the cabinet at the start and at the end?
route.why_this_ask: Find actual displacement instead of inferring motion from the push or elapsed time.
route.model_answer: At the same position, so s=0 m.

route.ask: What signed work follows from the measured displacement?
route.why_this_ask: Complete the work calculation and units.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Core1A reveals a fixed-wall example; Core1B independently elicits the zero-displacement decision from time-versus-displacement information without copying its values.

boundary_test.prompt: The same 75 N push moves the cabinet 0.20 m right in a later interval. Assuming the force remains constant and rightward over that displacement, what is its work on the cabinet?
boundary_test.answer: +15 J, since W=75 N×0.20 m for aligned force and displacement. The zero-work conclusion changes once displacement becomes nonzero.
boundary_test.confirms: Zero work was caused by zero displacement, not by a supposed inability of a contact push to do work.

predict.prompt: A powered rigid cart moves 3 m right on level ground in the ground frame under a constant 22 N drive force right, a constant 7 N resistance left, and vertical weight and support forces. What is the work of each force and their total?
predict.defensible_answer: The drive contributes +66 J, resistance −21 J, and vertical weight and support each 0 J; adding the four same-cart contributions gives +45 J.

attempt.produces: Give the ground-frame signed work and total for the cart, stating all four force agents/directions, displacement and units, and supply an independent check using the along-path resultant.
attempt.model_response: On the cart over 3 m right in ground frame: drive work=+22×3=+66 J; resistance=−7×3=−21 J; support=0 J and weight=0 J since vertical. Total=+45 J. Parallel resultant=22−7=15 N, and 15×3=+45 J. Drive work alone is not total.

rubric.criterion: Declares body, forces, frame and displacement.
rubric.evidence_of: Cart; drive, resistance, support, gravity; ground; 3 m right.

rubric.criterion: Computes four signed work contributions.
Adds work and checks with the along-path resultant.
rubric.evidence_of: +45 J, independently 15 N×3 m=45 J.

rejected: The motor does +66 J, so total work is +66 J. Incorrect: the resisting force does −21 J, and work must be added by force.

route.ask: What is the same displacement for all forces acting on the cart?
Which force arrows are aligned with the displacement, opposed, or vertical?
route.why_this_ask: Use direction to determine signed components.
route.model_answer: Drive right, resistance left, support and weight vertical.

route.ask: How do individual work terms combine?
Can the net along-path force confirm this sum?

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Core1A reveals an individual-force ledger; this cycle requires the learner to generate and cross-check the ledger with a different force inventory.

boundary_test.prompt: If resistance rises to 22 N while all other forces and displacement remain the same, what is total work?
boundary_test.answer: 0 J; +66 J and −66 J cancel, even though each is nonzero.
boundary_test.confirms: Zero total does not imply zero individual force work.

predict.prompt: Beyond Grade 9, given: A box travels 6 m right in 4 s in the ground frame while constant horizontal forces of 3 N right and 3 N left act on it. In a supplied steady co-moving inertial frame, the box’s displacement over this interval is 0 m. What is the work of each force and the total in each frame?
predict.defensible_answer: For the box, ground-frame work is +18 J by the 3 N rightward contact force and −18 J by the 3 N leftward resistance; the total is 0 J. In the given steady co-moving inertial frame its displacement is 0 m, so each force does 0 J and total remains 0 J.

attempt.produces: Give both signed work totals and each force’s contribution, naming the box, acting agents, common time interval, given displacements and units in each of the two specified frames; explain any difference.
attempt.model_response: Target box; platform→box contact +3 N right and resistance agent→box −3 N left, balanced. Ground frame: 6 m right, works +18 J and −18 J, total 0 J. In the box’s steady co-moving inertial frame, displacement is 0 m, so both works 0 J and total 0 J. Frame and displacement must be reported with each result.

rubric.criterion: Declares target, both forces, interval and frames.
rubric.evidence_of: Box; two opposed 3 N forces; 4 s; ground and co-moving inertial.

rubric.criterion: Determines displacement in each frame.
rubric.evidence_of: Ground +6 m; co-moving 0 m.

rubric.criterion: Computes individual signed works and sums in both frames.
rubric.evidence_of: Ground +18 and −18 J sum 0; co-moving 0 and 0 J sum 0.

rubric.criterion: Interprets why individual work results differ without changing forces.
rubric.evidence_of: Displacement depends on the declared reference frame.

accepted: The ground observer finds +18 J and −18 J; the co-moving observer finds 0 J and 0 J.
rejected: The contact force does +18 J in both frames because the force is the same. Incorrect: the co-moving displacement is zero.

route.ask: Whose displacement matters for each force?
What is the box’s displacement during the same interval in each frame?
route.model_answer: 6 m right in ground frame, 0 m co-moving.

route.ask: What does each frame then give for work and total?

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: Unlike Core1A’s vehicle comparison, the learner must independently select the two displacements and compute both force ledgers across a longer event with a different contact pairing.

boundary_test.prompt: Still using only the ground frame, a box moves 2 m LEFT under two opposing horizontal forces, 4 N right and 4 N left. Calculate each work and the total; explain why the net work remains zero even though both contributions are nonzero.
boundary_test.answer: Rightward force does −8 J, leftward force does +8 J, and total is 0 J. The signed works cancel; a zero sum does not make either contribution zero.
boundary_test.confirms: The learner can use a declared ground displacement to reason from individual signs to a total without any moving-frame dynamics.
